title: The TRUE Payback Time for Heat Pumps
summary: UK boiler and heat pump installer weighs retrofit heat pump costs, running costs, the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, payback maths, servicing and lifespan against gas boilers.

assertions.quote: compared to the what two and a half grand for a typical kind of boiler swap
it's probably much cheaper in most cases to have a heat pump than it is gas boiler in a new build

verdicts.note: New builds avoid retrofit work and may avoid a gas connection, but the saving depends on the connection cost and design.

RMI finds heat pumps usually the lowest-cost option in new construction because one device replaces furnace and AC, with avoided gas mains and service (median $8,800 per home) adding to the advantage.

In Canadian modelling, heat pumps with electric backup are already the lowest lifetime-cost option in all new builds in Vancouver, Montreal and Halifax and for new detached homes in Toronto; this compares lifetime cost against gas plus AC, not upfront cost against a boiler.

assertions.quote: poor heat pump installations will cost 25 more than an old inefficient boiler
new efficient heat pump systems designed well and installed well will be 32 percent more efficient or cheaper to run
heat pumps can make use of time of use tariffs
allows you to store free solar power driving your costs down even more
if you've got a new working boiler the argument for having a heat pump is much much lower
deduct the cost of what you would have spent replacing your boiler with a newer model

verdicts.note: Standard incremental-cost analysis compares against the replacement you would buy anyway when equipment is due.
The study counts only the extra cost of a heat pump over replacing the existing heater with a similar one, assuming purchase at end of the old heater's life.

Wilson's consumer economics compare heat pump installation with a reference scenario of like-for-like replacement of equipment at end of lifetime, and find a majority of households can benefit against that reference; the shares are therefore the replacement-time case, not early replacement of working equipment.

Bernard et al. put the average Boiler Upgrade Scheme install at £12,713 total (private spend plus subsidy), £5,213 private, and count it against a £2,250 gas boiler the household would buy anyway, so the cost they weigh is the extra over the replaced system; a modelling assumption, not a test of the rule.

assertions.quote: currently we have the bus or boiler upgrade screen which brings down your return investment by another 5k
the value of your property would have increased
roughly 100 to 300 pounds plus v80 for a heat pump service
heat pumps life should be more like 20 years
the vast majority of work is putting in pipe and installing radiators

verdicts.note: Labour and soft costs dominate retrofit prices, but countries with mature markets show those costs can fall with scale and standard designs.
For US ductless heat pumps, labour is commonly 30-35% of total cost (radiators do not apply to air-to-air systems).
